page.layout: One column of italic text, centred on the page, followed by a closing line with a signature block below it: "V. E.", then the greeting "studiosissimè colens", then the name "M. LUDOVICUS LUCIUS." Foot of the page: a gathering mark with a page number at the right.

p.i: est, invito & provoco. Vobis porrò Viris Excel-lentissimis, hæsce chartulas submissè offero ac de-dico: non quòd abs me V. E. dignum quidquam proficisci posse exi'stimem: verùm ut jam diu & adhuc debiti mei erga Vos grati animi ac obser-vantiæ notam ponã, quos & Parentum, & Præ-ceptorum ⁊ Mæcenatúmq; nomine mihi perpetuò habeo observandos colendosq;. Vos quæso, ut eo animo excipiatis hoc meum propositum, quo vos facturos non dubito, hoc est, favente ac benevo-lo: idq; si opus fuerit vestrâ autoritate ac patroci-nio defendatis. Deum ego summum exoro, ut V. E. ea omnia quæ ad vitam & pietatem pertinēt, abundè elargiatur, ad Nominis sui SS. gloriam, Patriæq; nostræ almæ ornamentum et emolumen-tum. Amen. Perscriptum Basileæ, 8. Kal. Octobr. ⁊ Anni Christianæ epochæ 1597.

page.notes: The "1597" is printed with spaced digits. The ornamental flourishes before "Mæcenatúmq;" and before "Anni" are decorative marks, not letters, and are only approximated here. The "est" at the start is printed with a long s, shown here as a plain s. The printed signature mark at the foot reads "A" with "4" beside it; it is transcribed as the gathering signature "A 4", and the page number is taken as 4. The word "facturos" is printed with a long s in the middle of the word and is read as "facturos". The "⁊" marks are printed flourishes and are kept as they appear.
